en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Thirteenth Chapter
The Discussion on One Who Has Attained Relishing:
Does one who has attained relish? Is craving for jhāna the object of jhāna?
Yes, it is.
Is that jhāna the object of that jhāna?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is that jhāna the object of that jhāna?
“Yes, he does.
By that contact he contacts that contact; by that feeling he feels that feeling;
by that perception he perceives that perception; by that volition he intends that volition; by that consciousness he cognizes that consciousness.”
"Does one think that thought by means of that thought; does one examine that examination by means of that examination;
does one love that rapture by means of that rapture; does one remember that mindfulness by means of that mindfulness; does one understand that wisdom by means of that wisdom?
"One should certainly not say so... [and so on].
Is craving for jhāna associated with consciousness? Is jhāna associated with consciousness?
Yes. [The same applies to] two types of contact... [and so on].
Is there a conjunction of two states of consciousness?
One should not say so… [as before] … Is attachment to jhāna unwholesome, while jhāna itself is wholesome?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright with their counterparts, come into manifestation?
You should not speak thus …pe… .
"Are wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and superior states, dark and bright states with their counterparts, present before one?
"Yes.
"Has it not been said by the Blessed One:"
“Bhikkhus, there are these four things that are very far apart. Which four?
The sky and the earth, bhikkhus—”
“This is the first [instance of] that which is very far, very far away … [as before] … Therefore, the Dhamma of the virtuous is far from the wicked.
Is this indeed a Sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said that "wholesome and unwholesome,
blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterparts-dhammas come into manifestation.
It should not be so stated.
“Does one who has attained [jhāna] relish it? Is attachment to jhāna directed toward jhāna as its object?
— “Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Here, monks, a monk, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna; he relishes it, desires it, and finds satisfaction in it.
With the stilling of applied and sustained thought... [he enters] the second jhāna...
[he enters] the third jhāna...”
“He enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna; he relishes it, desires it, and finds satisfaction in it.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
"Therefore, one who has attained [jhāna] relishes it; the craving for jhāna has jhāna as its object.
The discussion on whether one who has attained relishes [jhāna] is finished.
